VI. Elegantia poëtica & musica.
§. 1. Est in hoc carmine singularis elegantia poëtica,
inventionem spectans, & scenam repræsenta-
minis egregiè adornans, dum omne argumentum inter
plures canentium sibique invicem respondentium personas
dividit. Primæ & ultimæ orationis vices videntur
mihi spectare ad Prophetam ipsum, duæ intermediæ ad
eos, qui à Propheta excitati jam ostendunt se ex dato
fundamento didicisse, & etiamnum tenere ulteriorem viarum
Dei collationem, qui proinde Prophetæ succentu-

page.notes: Left edge has a dark stain and the book's binding edge; not text. The word after "N. T." is partly obscured by a mark, so "necessariam" is uncertain. "graviam" in the top line is read as "gratiam" but is doubtful. "contimuisse" is hard to read; the letters are unclear and may be "continuisse". The asterisk-like mark after "futurae" is a printed symbol, transcribed as *. Hyphenated line-end words keep their printed hyphens.
